strengths.text: Supports OpenAI Realtime speech-to-speech models (gpt-realtime-2025-08-28 listed as production); docs list knowledge bases and custom voice cloning as unsupported in that mode.

Provider choice is explicit and language coverage is stated per provider: STT Deepgram 100+, Google 125+, Gladia 110+, AssemblyAI 18 languages; TTS Vapi 40+, Azure 140+, ElevenLabs 30+, OpenAI 50+, PlayHT 80+, with automatic language detection.

SIP: a Vapi SIP phone number accepts inbound calls from any SIP client; outbound calls need an imported number (for example Twilio) or your own SIP trunk. Docs list US and EU regions with separate API and SIP hosts.

Pricing page lists provider-billed transport rates (Twilio inbound $0.008/min, outbound $0.014/min; Telnyx $0.0055/min; Vonage $0.00814/min) and shows no Vapi charge for Vapi Telephony/SIP, WebSockets or Daily WebRTC.

limits.text: No Success Package tier includes 4 concurrent calls, 14 days raw data retention and email support without an SLA; extra concurrency is $10 per line per month.
When all concurrency slots are in use, new calls are blocked (the API returns concurrencyBlocked = true); capacity comes from the package plus paid add-on lines.
HIPAA is a paid compliance add-on that requires a signed BAA and approved HIPAA-compliant model, voice and transcription providers.

Docs list SSO as not included in Usage only, Core or Pro (custom on Premier) and say Success Packages are available to new customers while existing accounts see no change 'right now', so the pricing page may not describe every account's terms.

derived_notes: DERIVED (my arithmetic from OpenAI's stated token rates; OpenAI states no per-minute estimate for gpt-realtime-* on the pricing or model pages): user audio 10 tokens/s = 600 tokens/min; assistant audio 20 tokens/s = 1,200 tokens/min. gpt-realtime-2.1 audio: input 600 x $32.00/1M = $0.0192/min, output 1,200 x $64.00/1M = $0.0768/min. gpt-realtime-2.1-mini audio: input 600 x $10.00/1M = $0.0060/min, output 1,200 x $20.00/1M = $0.0240/min. These count only new audio tokens. OpenAI states the whole conversation is re-sent as input on every response (cached audio rate $0.40/1M when the cache hits), and text tokens (instructions, tool calls, reasoning) and input transcription are extra, so real cost per minute is higher and grows with session length. The only per-minute figures on the OpenAI pricing page are GPT-Live ($0.05/min) and the transcription/translation models.

strengths.text: Connection options documented: WebRTC (unified POST /v1/realtime/calls or ephemeral keys from /v1/realtime/client_secrets) and WebSocket (wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2.1).
SIP: point a SIP trunk at sip.api.openai.com (sip-eu.api.openai.com for European data residency); a webhook (realtime.call.incoming) fires per call.
Turn detection: server_vad (threshold, prefix_padding_ms, silence_duration_ms; default) and semantic_vad (eagerness low, medium, high, auto); VAD can be turned off.
Vendor states /v1/realtime storage and processing regions are United States and Europe (EEA + Switzerland) for gpt-realtime, -1.5, -mini, -2, -2.1 and -2.1-mini.

derived_notes: DERIVED (my arithmetic): Agent Platform pricing page states 25 audio tokens/second = 1,500 tokens/min. Audio input 1,500 x $3.00/1M = $0.0045/min; audio output 1,500 x $12.00/1M = $0.0180/min. The Gemini API page itself shows $0.005/min (input, rounded) and $0.018/min (output), so the two sources agree. If the general 32 tokens/s figure on the Gemini API tokens page applied to Live audio, input would be 1,920 tokens/min x $3.00/1M = $0.00576/min; I did not use it because the Live pages state per-minute figures and 25 tokens/s. Google states the full session context window is billed on every turn, so longer sessions cost more per minute than these figures; image/video frames and text are extra.

strengths.text: Protocol: stateful WebSocket; server-to-server or client-to-server (ephemeral tokens recommended); audio in as 16 kHz PCM, out as 24 kHz PCM; partner integrations over WebRTC/WebSockets include LiveKit, Pipecat by Daily, Voximplant, Agora, Stream Vision Agents.

Automatic VAD is on by default and configurable (prefixPaddingMs, silenceDurationMs; docs recommend 500-800 ms, server default about 800 ms); manual activityStart/activityEnd signals or disabling VAD are supported.
gemini-3.8-live: 131,072 input / 65,536 output token limits; asynchronous function calling is the default; Google Search grounding supported; Batch API and context caching not supported.
Vendor states (Agent Platform) gemini-3.8-live is available in multi-region us and eu and in us-central1, and lists data residency, CMEK and VPC-SC as security controls.

limits.text: Without context window compression, audio-only sessions are limited to 15 minutes and audio+video to 2 minutes; a connection lasts about 10 minutes, so long calls need session resumption (Gemini API docs: resumption tokens valid 2 hours).
Agent Platform: up to 1,000 concurrent sessions per project on pay-as-you-go (not for Provisioned Throughput); resume a session within 24 hours; default conversation session 10 minutes.

Session context window: 128k tokens for native audio output models, 32k for other Live API models; native audio models return AUDIO only (text via output transcription); the capabilities page still carries a 'Preview' banner although the changelog lists 3.8 Live as GA.
Google's pages disagree on supported language count: 70 (Gemini API Live overview), 99 (Gemini API capabilities page), 24 (Agent Platform Live overview); both recorded, none resolved.

strengths.text: Docs: the framework adds any Python or Node.js program to LiveKit rooms as a realtime participant, offers LiveKit Agent Builder for no-code prototyping and deployment in the browser, and includes agent server orchestration, load balancing and Kubernetes compatibility; docs state the framework and the LiveKit ecosystem are Apache 2.0.

Python (livekit/agents) and Node.js (livekit/agents-js) SDKs; the Python repo has 77 subdirectories under livekit-plugins/ and the Node repo 38 under plugins/ (counted 2026-09-30; includes provider plugins and helpers such as turn-detector).

Pricing page lists WebRTC transport, SIP telephony (third-party trunks, rentable US local and toll-free numbers) and a Twilio connector that bridges Twilio Programmable Voice calls into LiveKit rooms.
Turn-detector and adaptive-interruption models are free for agents deployed to LiveKit Cloud; local development gets 7,500 and 40,000 free requests per month respectively on every plan.

limits.text: Build plan: deployed agents can be shut down after sessions end and take 10 to 20 seconds to start again; allowances are hard caps and are shared across a user's free projects.
Concurrency caps: agent sessions 5 (Build), 20 (Ship), up to 600 on Scale (starts at 50); LiveKit Inference concurrency 5, 20 and 50; Build allows 100 participants.
Agent build context upload limit is 1 GB per deployment; observability data has a 30-day retention window; Server API rate limit 1,000 requests per minute.
Role-based access, region pinning, HIPAA and security reports start at the $500/mo Scale plan; SSO, shared Slack and support SLA are Enterprise.

strengths.text: gpt-live-transcribe returns streaming transcript deltas in Realtime transcription sessions (session type 'transcription'); `audio.input.transcription.delay` accepts minimal, low, medium, high or xhigh, and the session supports `languages`, `keywords` and `prompt` hints.
gpt-transcribe handles files (up to 25 MB) and committed turns in Realtime sessions, accepts prompt, keywords and languages, and returns detected languages.
gpt-realtime-whisper is priced by audio duration (per minute) rather than text tokens; gpt-live-transcribe and gpt-transcribe model pages show the same per-minute audio-duration pricing.
Rate limits for gpt-live-transcribe by usage tier: Tier 1 500 RPM / 60,000 TPM, Tier 2 2,000 RPM / 210,000 TPM; Free not supported.

limits.text: In gpt-live-transcribe sessions `turn_detection` must be omitted or null: the model does not support server_vad or semantic_vad, so the application has to supply turn boundaries.
gpt-live-transcribe returns no word-level timestamps, speaker labels or confidence scores, and no detected-language predictions (gpt-transcribe returns detected languages).
The pages opened give no language count for gpt-live-transcribe or gpt-transcribe (they list accepted code formats: ISO 639-1, selected ISO 639-3, zh locales); whisper-1 is described as 98 languages.

gpt-realtime-whisper and gpt-live-transcribe are both listed as streaming STT at $0.017/minute; the guide recommends gpt-live-transcribe and the pages opened do not explain how the two differ beyond model-card ratings.

what_it_is: Google Cloud managed speech recognition API. The v2 API provides gRPC streaming recognition (StreamingRecognize) with the chirp_2 and chirp_3 multilingual models next to older models such as latest_long and phone_call.
best_for: Teams already on Google Cloud that want managed streaming STT with voice-activity events and stream timeouts in one API.

Streaming recognition is available through gRPC only; voice activity events exist only for StreamingRecognize gRPC requests.

strengths.text: Bidirectional Media Streams via <Connect><Stream>: the WebSocket server receives the inbound track and can send base64 audio/x-mulaw at 8000 Hz back into the call, plus 'mark' and 'clear' messages to track or flush queued audio.

SIP REFER is supported on SIP call legs: inbound REFER sent to Programmable Voice (blind transfer; the Refer-To header is limited to 256 characters) and outbound <Refer>; it works when at least one call leg is a SIP connection.
Recording: Twilio states two-party Voice recordings are dual-channel by default; recording is $0.0025/min on the pricing page.
Vendor states compliance certifications HIPAA, GDPR, PCI, SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001 (pricing page FAQ).

limits.text: Default 1 CPS for Programmable Voice API calls per account; inbound calls are not limited by CPS; new accounts without an approved Business Profile cannot self-serve CPS increases.

Bidirectional streams: one Stream per call, only the inbound track is received, DTMF is inbound only (a server cannot send DTMF), and a bidirectional stream cannot be started with the Stream resource (use <Connect><Stream>). Unidirectional streams share a four-track limit with SIPREC, Real-Time Transcription and Answering Machine Detection.
Audio sent back must be base64 mulaw at 8000 Hz without file headers; if buffered audio passes 10 minutes Twilio stops accepting more audio for that Stream (warning 31931).
Outbound <Refer> works only on SIP call legs; PSTN and Twilio Voice SDK legs are not supported and return an error.

limits.text: Default 1 CPS per trunk per region for termination; raising it to 1-5 per trunk costs a monthly fee and requires traffic with average call duration above 30 s, at most 10% of calls at or under 12 s and ASR above 70%; above 5 CPS requires sales.
REFER is blind transfer only; early media with call transfers is not supported; transfers to emergency services (911/933) are not supported.
Twilio sizes trunk bandwidth at about 100 kbps per simultaneous call (G.711 plus overhead), so peak bandwidth must be provisioned on the customer side.
Limited Availability codecs (G.729, Opus, AMR-NB) require contacting Twilio sales.

strengths.text: Bidirectional media streaming: stream_url (wss) with stream_bidirectional_mode 'rtp'; codecs PCMU 8 kHz (default), PCMA, G722, OPUS, AMR-WB and L16 16 kHz; audio chunks of 20 ms to 30 s; a 'clear' message flushes queued audio.

Call-control commands include transfer, SIP REFER ('Send a SIP REFER request for a call'), bridge, record_start/stop/pause/resume, streaming_start/stop, transcription_start and ai_assistant_start; Conversation Relay (Telnyx) uses a single bidirectional WebSocket per session.

SIP trunking docs include configuration guides for LiveKit and for OpenAI GPT-Live; the GPT-Live guide sets TLS signalling and mandatory SRTP and keeps call media on the Telnyx-to-OpenAI SIP path (the app does not relay audio).
Vendor states a 99.99% uptime guarantee (SLA JSON linked from the Telnyx docs index).

limits.text: Default limit of 30 dials per second, evaluated as a 5-second rolling sum (150); over-limit dials return HTTP 429 with code 90103; higher limits by request to support.
Outbound concurrent call limit is global to the account: 2 at initial setup, 10 after Level 2 verification, more via support (documented on the SIP trunking concurrent-limits page).

Only one streaming/fork operation per call, and one bidirectional stream per call; media files sent over the WebSocket must be base64 mp3 and can be submitted once per second; audio in a different encoding than the call is transcoded.
Rates vary by destination and volume tier; carrier passthrough and taxes vary by destination (pricing page).

strengths.text: WebSocket connector: an NCCO 'connect' action with a websocket endpoint streams caller audio as binary frames (16-bit linear PCM at 8, 16 or 24 kHz, about 20 ms per packet) and accepts audio and JSON commands back; optional handshake authorization (Vonage JWT or custom header).

Recording: NCCO record supports MP3, OGG or WAV at 16 kHz, split stereo (caller and callee on separate channels) and multichannel up to 32 legs; recordings are stored by Vonage for 30 days, then deleted.
SIP trunking supports codecs PCMA, PCMU, iLBC, g729, g722 and Speex16; TLS 1.2 on port 5061 and SRTP (AES_CM_128_HMAC_SHA1_80).
Vonage publishes a guide for building an AI voice agent with the Voice API and Deepgram's Voice Agent (barge-in supported).

limits.text: Default 3 CPS for outbound calls; inbound calls are not limited; each outbound phone, sip, websocket or app leg counts, including each WebSocket connection; over the limit returns 429 (REST) or 503 (SIP); higher limits on request.
SIP REFER support is not described in the Voice API and SIP pages opened; call transfer is documented through PUT /calls/{uuid} (transfer) and NCCO actions.
Some US zone-based outbound rates are available only by contacting sales.
Call transcription is a chargeable feature with a 2-hour maximum limit for transcribing voice calls (NCCO reference).

strengths.text: Voice API v2 documents Voice Stream: a WebSocket API for bidirectional PCM audio on calls, with flexible chunk sizes (20 ms or larger), a clear command that discards unplayed buffered audio, and a 5 MB per-call buffer limit.

Vendor states (LiveKit blog, 2026-06-17) that v1 is the strongest model in LiveKit's own evaluation; LiveKit's eot-bench README (published by LiveKit, repo pushed 2026-09-16) lists English false-cutoff rates at a 300 ms budget of 9.9% (v1), 27.8% (v1-mini), 12.9% (Deepgram Flux), 35.2% (SmartTurn v3.2). This is a vendor benchmark of its own model.
Text model card: CPU-only INT8 ONNX, under 500 MB RAM, 14 languages, per-language thresholds; docs give about 50-160 ms per-turn CPU latency and 396 MB on disk for the text model.
Open test data: eot-bench harness and dataset (real human-to-agent turns, 14 languages) are published under Apache-2.0 so other models can be measured the same way.

limits.text: License restricts the model weights to use with the LiveKit Agents framework (not standalone, not other frameworks) and bars using outputs to train non-LiveKit models.
Full v1 needs network access to LiveKit Inference; local fallback v1-mini runs in a shared CPU process and docs advise compute-optimized instances rather than burstable ones to avoid timeouts.
Text model is deprecated, text-only (no prosody), needs an STT model, and its context is limited to 128 tokens across up to 6 turns.
The audio detector requires VAD with min_silence_duration of at least 0.25 s; without an STT language it defaults to English thresholds.

name: Pipecat Smart Turn
activity_evidence: Pipecat docs page (opened 2026-09-30) states Smart Turn v3 with LocalSmartTurnAnalyzerV3 is the default user-turn stop strategy since Pipecat v0.0.102; pipecat-ai/pipecat v1.12.0 released 2026-09-26 (GitHub API). what_it_is: Open-source audio-native end-of-turn model (Whisper Tiny encoder plus linear head, about 8M parameters; current release v3.2) that classifies whether a user's turn is complete from raw 16 kHz audio once VAD detects silence.
best_for: Pipecat users (it is bundled and on by default) and anyone who wants a permissively licensed, self-hosted, multilingual end-of-turn model that runs on CPU.
pricing_model: Free, open source; runs locally (ONNX).
headline_price: Free (BSD-2-Clause); no hosted fee. Pipecat Cloud has a separate guide page for running it.

strengths.text: README lists 23 languages: Arabic, Bengali, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, German, English, Finnish, French, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Marathi, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese.

Vendor states inference runs in as little as 10 ms on some CPUs and under 100 ms on most cloud instances, about 65 ms on a Pipecat Cloud standard 1x instance; model size 8 MB int8 (CPU) or 32 MB fp32 (GPU).
Audio native: takes 16 kHz mono PCM (up to 8 seconds, padded at the start) and uses prosody, not a transcript; run only during silence after a lightweight VAD such as Silero.
Bundled with pip package pipecat-ai (no separate download); SmartTurnParams defaults: stop_secs 3.0, pre_speech_ms 500, max_duration_secs 8.0.

limits.text: Needs VAD (Pipecat docs recommend VAD stop_secs 0.2); not designed for very short audio segments, and must be re-run on the whole turn if more speech arrives.

Benchmarks from competing vendors rank it below their own models: LiveKit's eot-bench README (2026-09) lists SmartTurn v3.2 at 35.2% false cutoffs at a 300 ms budget vs 9.9% for LiveKit v1; Krisp's blog (updated May 2026) also compares it. Both are vendor-run.
Model card metadata tags the pipeline as voice-activity-detection although the project describes it as turn detection; no newer weights than v3.2 were found on the Hub on 2026-09-30.

name: Deepgram Flux end-of-turn detection
activity_evidence: Deepgram changelog entries dated 2026-09-25 (mid-stream numerals toggle on Flux STT), 2026-09-14 and 2026-08-28 (flexible turn-taking control / ForceEndTurn); pricing page opened 2026-09-30.
what_it_is: Turn detection built into Deepgram's Flux streaming speech-to-text models (flux-general-en, flux-general-multi) on the /v2/listen WebSocket; the model emits EagerEndOfTurn, TurnResumed and EndOfTurn events governed by eot_threshold, eager_eot_threshold and eot_timeout_ms.
best_for: Teams using Deepgram STT who want end-of-turn decisions from the STT stream and the option to start LLM calls early (eager end-of-turn).
license: proprietary (hosted API; self-hosted deployment offered per docs)
pricing_model: Per-minute streaming STT pricing; turn detection is part of Flux, with no separate line item shown.
headline_price: Flux English: $0.0065/min pay-as-you-go current price (regular $0.0077/min); Flux Multilingual: $0.0078/min pay-as-you-go. Page notes limited-time promotional rates on streaming.

strengths.text: Configurable: eot_threshold 0.5-1.0 (default 0.7); eager_eot_threshold 0.3-0.9 (unset by default, enables EagerEndOfTurn and TurnResumed; must be <= eot_threshold); eot_timeout_ms 500-60000 (default 5000). eot_threshold=1.0 suppresses native end-of-turn so the client drives turns with ForceEndTurn.
Vendor states about 260 ms end-of-turn detection; EagerEndOfTurn transcript matches the later EndOfTurn transcript unless a TurnResumed event cancels it.
Flux Multilingual (flux-general-multi) supports 10 languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Russian, Portuguese, Japanese, Italian, Dutch, with optional language_hint.
Client can override: ForceEndTurn message and Configure message allow switching between automatic, semi-manual and manual turn ending mid-session (changelog 2026-08-28).

limits.text: Eager mode increases LLM calls and requires handling speculative generation and TurnResumed cancellations (docs list this as a trade-off).
Flux requires the /v2/listen endpoint (not /v1/listen); docs strongly recommend 80 ms audio chunks.

LiveKit's eot-bench README (LiveKit-published, 2026-09) lists Deepgram Flux at 12.9% English false cutoffs at a 300 ms budget and 1151 ms endpointing latency at a 5% cutoff; Krisp's blog notes Flux English is English-only. Both are competitor-run benchmarks.

activity_evidence: AssemblyAI pricing reference document (served at assemblyai.com/pricing) states 'Last updated: 2026-09-28'; docs pages opened 2026-09-30 describe Universal-3.6 Pro Streaming.
what_it_is: End-of-turn detection inside AssemblyAI's streaming speech-to-text. Universal-3.6 Pro decides from the transcript plus silence windows (min_turn_silence, max_turn_silence, preset by mode); Universal-Streaming uses an end_of_turn_confidence_threshold plus silence timers. A ForceEndpoint message lets you supply your own turn logic.
best_for: Teams using AssemblyAI streaming STT who want transcript-aware endpointing with tunable silence windows, including mid-stream changes while a caller dictates a phone number or address.
license: proprietary (hosted API; self-hosted streaming exists per docs index)

strengths.text: Universal-3.6 Pro defaults by mode: min_turn_silence 128 ms (min_latency, balanced) or 512 ms (max_accuracy); max_turn_silence 640, 1280 or 2560 ms; vad_threshold 0.2; interruption_delay 0/500/500 ms. Values can be updated mid-stream with UpdateConfiguration.

Universal Streaming models use end_of_turn_confidence_threshold (default 0.4) with min_turn_silence 400 ms, max_turn_silence 1280 ms and vad_threshold 0.4; docs give aggressive, balanced and conservative presets.

name: Speechmatics end-of-utterance and Agent STT turn detection
activity_evidence: Speechmatics release notes list Realtime SaaS releases on 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-16 and Batch SaaS on 2026-09-30 (changelog opened 2026-09-30).
what_it_is: Two mechanisms: the Realtime API's end_of_utterance_silence_trigger (server-side word-timing silence countdown that sends EndOfUtterance), and Agent STT (model linden-1, /v2/agent) which sends StartOfTurn/EndOfTurn with turn_config.turn_detection_mode 'vad' (service decides) or 'external' (your app sends ForceEndOfUtterance).
best_for: Teams using Speechmatics STT (55+ languages) who want turn events from the API, or who want to keep their own turn detector (Pipecat, LiveKit) via the external mode.
license: proprietary (hosted; Agent STT is SaaS only per docs)
pricing_model: Per-hour speech-to-text pricing by model; no separate turn-detection fee shown.
headline_price: Agent STT model Linden 1: current price $0.16/hr (previous $0.21/hr); Real-time Standard $0.24/hr; Real-time Enhanced $0.43/hr (Pro column of the pricing table).

strengths.text: Realtime end_of_utterance_silence_trigger allows 0-2 seconds (0 disables); docs recommend 0.5-0.8 s for voice AI and 0.8-1.2 s for dictation.

Agent STT emits StartOfTurn on the first transcribed word (not first sound) and EndOfTurn after the final segment; 'external' mode turns off the service's VAD so Pipecat, LiveKit or push-to-talk can own turn endings via ForceEndOfUtterance.
Linden 1 supports the same languages as Realtime transcription (docs), with integrations for LiveKit, Pipecat and Vapi.

limits.text: In Agent STT 'vad' mode the turn decision comes from voice activity and docs state VAD is not currently configurable; ForceEndOfUtterance is unsupported there.
Agent STT is available on SaaS only, and Linden 1 is not available on the Batch or Realtime endpoints.
Realtime end-of-utterance is silence-based on word timings (no semantic or audio turn model documented on that page); the ML SMART_TURN option lived in the deprecated Voice SDK.

activity_evidence: Krisp turn-taking blog shows 'Updated May 2026'; krisp.ai/developers and krisp.ai/pricing opened 2026-09-30; LiveKit's pricing page (2026-09-30) and Pipecat docs list Krisp VIVA.
what_it_is: Proprietary server-side SDK from Krisp for voice agents with four separate models: voice isolation (krisp-viva-pro up to 32 kHz, krisp-viva-tel up to 16 kHz), Turn Prediction v3 (krisp-viva-tp-v3), Interruption Prediction v1 (krisp-viva-ip-v1) and VAD; also sold as background voice cancellation and noise cancellation inside LiveKit Cloud and Pipecat Cloud.
best_for: Agents that hear background speakers or noisy lines and want to add one vendor's isolation, audio-native turn prediction and backchannel-aware interruption detection, either through LiveKit Cloud or Pipecat Cloud or by applying for the SDK.
license: proprietary (SDK, models and API key from the Krisp developer portal)
pricing_model: Direct SDK: application or contact-sales plans (Early stage, Enterprise) with no public price; metered per minute when used through Pipecat Cloud or LiveKit Cloud.
headline_price: Direct from Krisp: contact sales / apply (no public price; Early stage and Enterprise 'volume pricing'). Through Pipecat Cloud: first 10,000 minutes per month free, then $0.0015/min. Through LiveKit Cloud: see voice isolation rows (included minutes, then $0.0012/min).

strengths.text: Vendor states (blog updated May 2026): Turn Prediction v3 is about 9M parameters, 30 MB, CPU inference, multilingual (English, German, French, Spanish, Hindi, Finnish, Italian, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian and more, 12+ languages); Interruption Prediction v1 is about 6M parameters, 24 MB, English only.

Interruption prediction separates backchannels ('uh-huh') from real interruptions; Krisp lists Python, Node.js, Go and iOS SDKs plus LiveKit and Pipecat support.

name: OpenAI Realtime API VAD modes (server_vad, semantic_vad)
activity_evidence: The Realtime VAD guide (opened 2026-09-30) documents both modes and names the transcription models gpt-live-transcribe and gpt-realtime-whisper; the OpenAI API changelog (opened 2026-09-30) has entries dated Sep 15 to Sep 29, 2026 (the ones read concern other models and APIs, not VAD; the guide page itself shows no date).
what_it_is: Turn-detection settings of the OpenAI Realtime API, chosen per session with session.audio.input.turn_detection: server_vad (silence-based chunking with threshold, prefix_padding_ms, silence_duration_ms) and semantic_vad (a classifier on the words said, with an eagerness setting of low, medium, high or auto).
best_for: Teams building on the OpenAI Realtime API (speech-to-speech or transcription sessions) that need to tune when a user turn is closed and when the model starts or interrupts a response.
pricing_model: No separate VAD charge on the guide; usage is billed under the Realtime model's own pricing (category B entries).
headline_price: Not applicable: VAD mode is a session setting and the VAD guide lists no separate price; model usage is priced per model (see category B).

strengths.text: server_vad exposes threshold (0 to 1), prefix_padding_ms and silence_duration_ms; the guide's example uses 0.5, 300 and 500, and lists create_response and interrupt_response flags for conversation mode.

semantic_vad scores the probability that the user has finished, based on the words said: a low probability waits for a timeout, a high probability does not wait; eagerness low, medium, high or auto (auto equals medium).

The API emits input_audio_buffer.speech_started and input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped events for either mode; the same turn_detection field applies to transcription sessions on models that support VAD.

limits.text: For gpt-live-transcribe and gpt-realtime-whisper, turn detection must be omitted or set to null and the client commits audio with input_audio_buffer.commit.
The guide describes both modes as server-side settings of the hosted API only; it gives no millisecond values for the low, medium and high eagerness timeouts.
server_vad chunks on periods of silence; the guide's advice for noisy environments is to raise the threshold (louder audio is then needed to activate).

name: Gemini Live API automatic activity detection
activity_evidence: Gemini API changelog (opened 2026-09-30) has an entry dated 2026-09-15 releasing gemini-3.8-live on the Live API and an entry dated 2026-08-26 for gemini-3.5-transcribe-live with multiple VAD strategies; the Live API capabilities guide (opened 2026-09-30) uses gemini-3.8-live in its examples.
what_it_is: Server-side voice activity detection in the Gemini Live API, on by default and configured through realtimeInputConfig.automaticActivityDetection (disabled, startOfSpeechSensitivity, endOfSpeechSensitivity, prefixPaddingMs, silenceDurationMs); it can be turned off so the client sends activity start and end signals itself.
best_for: Teams building voice agents on the Gemini Live API that need to tune start-of-speech and end-of-speech detection or take over activity signalling in their own client.
pricing_model: No separate VAD charge on the pages opened; usage is billed under the Live model's own pricing (category B entries).
headline_price: Not applicable: automatic activity detection is a session setting and the pages opened list no separate price; model usage is priced per model (see category B).

strengths.text: API reference lists start and end sensitivity enums (HIGH detects speech start or end more often, LOW less often), prefixPaddingMs (lower is more sensitive but raises false positives) and silenceDurationMs (larger allows longer speech gaps but adds latency).

Automatic VAD can be disabled with realtimeInputConfig.automaticActivityDetection.disabled set to true; the client then sends activityStart and activityEnd messages, and an interruption of the stream is marked by activityEnd instead of audioStreamEnd.
RealtimeInputConfig also carries activityHandling (what effect activity has) and turnCoverage (which input counts toward the user's turn).

limits.text: The automaticActivityDetection fields in the API reference are speech/non-speech controls with two-level sensitivity enums; no semantic end-of-turn setting is listed there.
If the audio stream is paused for more than a second, the guide says the client should send an audioStreamEnd event to flush cached audio.

name: WebRTC acoustic echo cancellation (AEC3 in libwebrtc; browser echoCancellation constraint)
activity_evidence: libwebrtc main tip commit dated 2026-09-30 (Gitiles JSON, unrelated to AEC); modules/audio_processing/aec3 directory present on main; MDN page for the echoCancellation constraint live 2026-09-30.
what_it_is: Two ways to get acoustic echo cancellation for a voice agent client: the AEC3 implementation in libwebrtc's modules/audio_processing/aec3 (adaptive FIR filter, FFT and related files), and the browser getUserMedia echoCancellation constraint, which asks the user agent to enable or disable echo cancellation.
best_for: Browser and WebRTC-based voice agents that need echo removed before audio reaches VAD, turn detection or STT; native apps that can build libwebrtc's audio processing.
pricing_model: Free; part of libwebrtc and of browsers.
headline_price: Free: open source library and browser feature.

strengths.text: MDN: the echoCancellation constraint can be true or false, and in browsers that support named types one type removes only echo of audio captured from remote peer-connection sources, which keeps locally shared audio.
libwebrtc's aec3 directory holds the AEC3 sources (files include adaptive_fir_filter.cc, aec3_fft.cc, aec3_common.cc).

limits.text: MDN: a plain constraint value is a request; the user agent attempts it but does not fail if it cannot be met, and only an exact value makes the request error when unmet.
Named echo-cancellation types depend on browser support; other browsers accept only true or false (MDN).

name: LiveKit Agents testing and Agent Simulations
activity_evidence: GitHub release livekit-agents@1.8.3 on 2026-09-26 and livekit-cli v2.18.8 on 2026-09-22; docs pages rendered 2026-09-30.
what_it_is: Testing built into LiveKit Agents: pytest/Vitest unit tests with LLM judges and tool mocks, plus Agent Simulations (beta) where an LLM-driven simulated user runs scenarios in text or audio mode on LiveKit Cloud and a judge grades the conversation.
best_for: Teams already building on LiveKit Agents that want tests and scenario simulations in the same SDK, CLI and CI, with text runs per commit and audio runs nightly.
license: Apache-2.0 (livekit/agents SDK including the unit-testing helpers, and LiveKit CLI); Agent Simulations execute on the hosted LiveKit Cloud service
open_source_notes: Unit-test helpers and judges ship in the Apache-2.0 livekit/agents repo. Simulations need a LiveKit Cloud project and the lk CLI authenticated to it; the simulator service is not open source.
pricing_model: LiveKit Cloud plans plus usage; no separate Agent Simulations price found
headline_price: No separate price found for Agent Simulations (beta); LiveKit Cloud Build $0/mo, Ship from $50/mo, Scale from $500/mo

strengths.text: Unit tests (pytest, Vitest) assert turn by turn on messages, tool calls and handoffs, with LLM judge(), tool mocking and CI support; the Python JudgeGroup runs several LLM judges at once, and LiveKit Agents ships eight built-in judges (for example accuracy and coherence).

Audio simulations report speech accuracy (word and character error rates) and responsiveness (end-to-end latency the caller heard, at p50, p95 and p99) and can degrade audio with --low-quality-microphone and --packet-loss.
Simulations run in parallel: 15 at once per run by default and a limit of 30 executing at once per project.
Agent observability is metered on LiveKit Cloud plans: Build includes 1,000 session-recording minutes and 100,000 events.

limits.text: Agent Simulations is BETA and needs a LiveKit Cloud project, LiveKit Agents 1.6.6+ (Python) or @livekit/agents 1.6.0+ (Node.js), and lk CLI v2.16.4+ for Python or v2.16.7+ for Node.js; audio simulations need v2.18.3+.
JudgeGroup and the full-conversation evaluation API are Python-only; Node.js shows no support in the docs.

arXiv abstract: bot-to-bot audio conversations with automatic simulation validation, 213 scenarios across three enterprise domains, and multi-trial measurements separating peak from reliable capability.
Perturbation suite applies background noises, user accents, simulated connection degradation and combined perturbations.
